title: Who Speaks Matters: Analysing the Influence of Linguistic Identity on Hate Classification
benchmark_measurement: The instability (measured as the percentage of classification flips) of hate speech detection models when the content targets specific religious groups. The study analyzed how classifications changed when explicit or implicit markers of a speaker's dialect/ethnicity were added to the input text.
findings: The stability of hate speech classification for content targeting religious groups is significantly affected by the speaker's dialect. The fine-tuned HateXplain-BERT model, for instance, showed a higher tendency to change its classification for content targeting religious groups when dialectal markers were introduced. In contrast, the GPT-4o model was more stable but still showed variability. The rate of these classification 'flips' also differed across religious groups; content targeting Buddhism showed lower flip rates, which the authors suggest might be due to a smaller number of samples for that category in the dataset.
references: AI@Meta. 2024. Llama 3 model card.
